headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors: Goose can read/write shared files and use MCP/network while ComfyUI is offline-only but can still be fed attacker-controlled artifacts.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, so it may ingest ComfyUI outputs or workflow files as trusted content. ComfyUI is asynchronous and handles workflows/files, creating a plausible bridge. This is not proven to be a default direct parser hijack, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Goose is configured to consume ComfyUI-generated workflow files or prompts from the shared filesystem
IF an MCP extension forwards ComfyUI output into Goose tool context without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable MCP extensions that ingest model outputs
Require manual review of any ComfyUI-generated text before Goose reads it
Use read-only mounts for ComfyUI output folders
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose reads and writes the user filesystem and sends data to configured model providers and MCP servers; ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model artifacts. If they share a workspace, sensitive assets can flow from ComfyUI into Goose and then to third parties. ComfyUI is offline by default, but Goose is not.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or output directory
IF Goose is pointed at a third-party model provider while reading ComfyUI artifacts
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs in a separate directory
Block Goose from accessing image/model artifact folders
Use a local-only model provider for Goose
Review and redact sensitive metadata before sharing files
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git, and MCP capabilities, while ComfyUI can also write files and uses an asynchronous queue. On a shared directory, concurrent edits can corrupt workflows, models, or git state. The overlap is dangerous by default because Goose supports multiple instances and shared state via filesystem.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory
IF Goose modifies git state while ComfyUI writes workflow or model files
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files
Avoid running Goose on repositories containing ComfyUI assets
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can act on files and external tools, so if it treats ComfyUI outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. ComfyUI can generate artifacts that Goose may summarize or operationalize without verification. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, but the blast radius is not inherently irreversible.
conditions: IF Goose uses ComfyUI-produced text, metadata, or workflow files as facts
IF Goose executes shell or subprocess actions based on unverified ComfyUI output
mitigations: Require human approval before Goose acts on ComfyUI output
Insert a verification step that checks outputs against source files
Limit Goose to read-only analysis of ComfyUI artifacts
Log every action derived from ComfyUI outputs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for exchanged artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: A compliance mismatch is plausible because Goose handles model-provider keys and broad network egress, while ComfyUI is offline and touches media/model assets. The main issue is policy drift on the same data class, not a proven residency or regulated-data violation. Only Goose is cited because the compliance risk is driven by its outbound handling.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive media is processed in ComfyUI and then sent by Goose to a remote provider
IF Goose retention or logging policies differ from the local ComfyUI workflow
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Goose prompts
Use local-only providers for Goose
Disable verbose logging for sensitive runs
Document retention rules for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: align data-handling policies
